written: 2026-10-21, committed BEFORE any generation or evaluation for this control (no ladder-generated piece exists yet).
audit_origin: the independent audit, round 1, finding F1: the whole-grid arm (candidate 9) and the carved-piece arms (candidates 10/11) used different scenario generators.
question: Within ONE generator (the ladder generator: load-only perturbation, PV |V| fixed, repo oracle), does the whole-vs-piece (size) contrast for UNSEEN families persist? i.e. are carved 150-950-bus pieces of the unseen families won by GENCO more often than the unseen whole grids when both are made by the same generator?
option_choice: Option (a) (whole grids through datakit default_pf) was ruled out by existing evidence: ladder_data runs on the unseen whole grids in data/external/genco-ladder/data/*/meta.json ended 'failed' (case2383wp_k after 5,704 s, case2868_rte, case3375wp_k), 'insufficient_valid_scenarios' with every generated sample a collapsed root (case2869_pegase 97/97, case2848_rte 1/1, case1888_rte, case1951_rte, case2746wp_k, case3012wp_k), so datakit default_pf cannot make usable unseen whole-grid data in the time available. Option (b) is therefore used: the carved pieces of BOTH families are regenerated through the ladder generator (powerflow_surrogate.generate load-only perturbation 0.8-1.2 global x 0.1 jitter, PV |V| fixed, verified AC solves) and converted by genco_challenge.ladder_to_datakit + pglib_rate_a_fix exactly as the whole-grid arm was.
piece_set: every piece that ran in candidate 10 (19 seen-family) and candidate 11 (17 unseen-family); a piece 'runs' here iff >= 20 usable ladder samples survive generation, conversion and the residual verification; the list of pieces that ran is written to protocol_ran.json after generation and BEFORE any GENCO or interpolator evaluation on them.
generator_details: ladder: 120 usable samples per piece targeted (seed 0), load-only perturbation, oracle-verified; conversion keeps the first 120 of a seeded draw, requires |dVm|<1e-6, |dVa|<1e-4 deg vs the stored label and a residual < 1e-6 pu; rate_a taken from the .m. Carved .m files are copied as pglib_opf_<piece>.m so the repo's pglib route is used.
evaluation: identical to candidates 9-11: GENCO zero-shot with candidate 7's mask, I1-I5 (same code), 3 mask seeds, 40% and 20% measured, noise-free, |V| MAE at unmeasured buses vs the label, ratio = median G / min median I, scenario-cluster bootstrap (2000, seed 7), win = ratio<1 and CI upper<1. graphkit test split test_ratio 0.99 intersected with verified labels.
comparisons: All win counts at 40% (primary) and 20% (secondary). Reused, not rerun: ladder-generated unseen whole grids (candidate 9: 17 grids, 8/17 at 40%, 3/17 at 20%) and ladder-generated seen whole grids (15 grids, 15/15 at 40%, 13/15 at 20%) from ../2026-10-21-genco-voltage-inference-oos/verdict.json.
primary_test: Fisher exact, one-sided: the proportion of ladder-generated UNSEEN-family PIECES where GENCO wins at 40% is HIGHER than the proportion of ladder-generated UNSEEN WHOLE grids (8/17), at p < 0.05 => 'size contrast persists within the ladder generator'; otherwise 'not shown'.
secondary_tests: same at 20% (unseen pieces vs unseen whole)
seen pieces (ladder) vs seen whole grids (ladder), one-sided, 40% and 20%
seen vs unseen PIECES within the ladder generator, two-sided Fisher, 40% and 20% (the family contrast at piece size, one generator)
descriptive: the same pieces under datakit (candidates 10/11) vs ladder: 2x2 table of win flags (generator effect on identical cut grids); median ratios

post_sentences.persists (p < 0.05): Within one generator (ladder), carved 150-950-bus pieces of the unseen families are won by GENCO more often than the unseen whole grids (X of N pieces vs 8 of 17 whole grids at 40%; one-sided Fisher p = P). So the whole-vs-piece contrast is not an artefact of the generator change between candidate 9 and candidates 10/11: wholeness or size of the grid, not only the scenario generator, separates them. This does not by itself say it is size (the pieces are also boundary-folded and OPF-screened), and it must be read with the seen-family whole grids that win 15/15, which neither size nor wholeness alone explains. Unaudited.
post_sentences.not shown (p >= 0.05): Within one generator (ladder), carved pieces of the unseen families are NOT won more often than the unseen whole grids (X of N vs 8 of 17 at 40%; one-sided Fisher p = P). The whole-vs-piece contrast of candidates 9 vs 11 is therefore not shown to survive a common generator and may be (partly) a generator effect. Unaudited.

caveats_preregistered: Pieces are not independent draws of a family (RTE = one parent case2848, Polish ~ one parent); the carved pieces' boundary injections are scaled by the ladder generator's load perturbation as well; ladder pieces whose generation fails are reported as not run, and failure rate is itself informative (the ladder generator has a loadability limit); pieces were OPF-screened (easier); the whole-grid arm used the PGLib/pandapower built-in networks of candidate 9 while the pieces use PGLib-derived carvings; unaudited.
